clue.text: Guards bags, getting one for nothing

indicators.note: getting introduces the change the word bags undergoes here
one for nothing means the one-letter takes the place of the nothing-letter

parts.note: to bag something is to pocket it, so bags gives the verb pockets
O is the zero-shaped letter standing for nothing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sentry pockets his loot, picking up a single item where before he had none.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' as a verb is POCKETS; 'getting one for nothing' swaps its O (nothing) for I (one). Guards is also a verb here: strikers' pickets guard a gate.
explanation.definitionFit: To picket a place is to stand watch over it, so pickets is a verb synonym of guards.

clue.text: Alcohol increase causes disturbance

parts.note: punch is a mixed alcoholic drink
to up something is to increase it

explanation.surface: More drink leads to trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch-up is a brawl or fight, an informal word for a violent disturbance.

clue.text: Deep Anglo-French connection?

parts.note: surface reading: a profound bond or friendship between Britain and France; setter's reading: a link laid literally deep, under the sea between the two countries

explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep' sounds like a close relationship, the entente cordiale, but it means physically deep underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal name for the Channel Tunnel, the rail link running beneath the English Channel.

clue.text: Number in that position ending on top

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting the ending on top moves the last letter of the word to the front

parts.note: there means in that place or position

explanation.surface: A figure sits in a particular slot, its final digit placed uppermost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a figure: it is something that makes you numb, an anaesthetic. 'ending on top' moves the final E of THERE to the top of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early anaesthetic, a substance that numbs, so it is literally a numb-er.

clue.text: Cleared luggage filling luxury ship lacking in character

indicators.note: a filling goes inside something, here into the phrase that follows

parts.note: to live in style is to live in luxury

indicators.note: something cleared is emptied out, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of luggage
SS is the prefix for a steamship

explanation.surface: Luggage is unloaded from a dull cruise liner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleared luggage' reads as passing customs, but it means the word stripped to its ends; 'luxury ship' splits into two pieces with the luggage between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something styleless has no flair or distinctive quality, so it is lacking in character.

clue.text: Celebrated ruler, first to back annex houses

indicators.note: the word for annex holds the other piece inside it, as a house holds its occupants

parts.note: to annex is to add or append something

indicators.note: the opening letter of the ruler's title moves to the end

parts.note: an emir is a Muslim ruler

explanation.surface: A famous ruler is first to support taking over buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First to back' sends the E of EMIR to the end, giving MIRE, which ADD then 'houses'. 'Annex houses' looks like a noun phrase about buildings, but annex is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated as a past-tense verb means praised or held in high regard, the same as admired.

clue.text: Look forward to drivers overtaking with charm

indicators.note: overtaking here means taking over, enclosing the short form of the next word

parts.note: the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
W is an abbreviation for with
it as in sex appeal or charm

explanation.surface: Charming drivers look forward to overtaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is a British motoring organisation, so it stands for drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to expect it or wait for it, a synonym of look forward to.

clue.text: Kind to boring flier in small chopper

indicators.note: boring into something means drilling inside it, so these pieces go in

parts.note: a moth is a flying insect
ilk means kind or sort
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kindly gesture towards an insect stuck in a small helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' suggests a helicopter or an axe, but it means a tooth; a child's tooth is small.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk tooth is a baby tooth, and teeth chop food, so a small chopper is a fair cryptic hint.

clue.text: Flustered magistrate forgetting mobile SIM in event on Thames?

indicators.note: a flustered person is in a muddle, so these letters are thrown into a new order
forgetting tells us some letters of the fodder are left out of the mix

parts.note: the SIM card in a mobile phone, giving the letters SIM

explanation.surface: A court official, in a fluster, has mislaid the SIM card from a phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' removes the S, I and M of the mobile SIM from MAGISTRATE, leaving AGTRATE, which 'Flustered' rearranges. The question mark admits a regatta can be held elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat races, like Henley's famous rowing event on the river.

clue.text: Justify aid from abroad being superior

indicators.note: in a down clue, being superior means being placed above, so the foreign piece goes first

parts.note: de is French for from
to serve someone is to aid them

explanation.surface: Foreign aid can be justified if the donor is better off.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve something is to merit it, to have a claim that warrants or justifies it.

clue.text: Bad time to abandon spruce that's rotten at heart

indicators.note: something at the heart of a word sits in its middle
abandoning means leaving behind, so one letter for time drops out

parts.note: spruce and natty both mean smartly dressed
T is the standard abbreviation for time
an exclamation of disgust at something rotten

explanation.surface: A spruce tree that has rotted through over time is in bad shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' looks like the tree, but it means smart. NATTY loses one T and UGH goes into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Naughty means badly behaved, so it can stand in for bad as an adjective describing conduct.

clue.text: Claims the entire perimeter excludes diameter

parts.note: the entire amount is all of it

indicators.note: excluding something means leaving it out, here the letter that abbreviates diameter

parts.note: the perimeter of a shape is made up of its edges
D is the usual abbreviation for diameter

explanation.surface: A geometry statement: the whole boundary of a circle leaves out its diameter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perimeter' and 'diameter' make the clue read as geometry; D is the standard abbreviation for diameter.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert without proof, so alleges is a synonym of claims as a verb.

clue.text: Most ambitious clergymen defrocked, previously suspended

indicators.note: previously places the suspended word before the clergymen

parts.note: something suspended is hung

indicators.note: stripped of their frocks, the clergymen lose their outer letters, leaving the inside

parts.note: priests are clergymen

explanation.surface: Churchmen who have been thrown out of the ministry were earlier suspended from duty.
explanation.walkthrough: To defrock a priest is to strip off the outer garments, so the clergymen lose their outermost letters; 'previously' puts the suspended word first.
explanation.definitionFit: The hungriest people are the most eager and driven, so in the figurative sense they are the most ambitious.

clue.text: Show annoyance with men in school

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval
other ranks, ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Pupils or staff grumble about the men in a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a noun but is the verb, to teach. OR (other ranks) is the crossword stock for men.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach them, which is what a tutor does as a verb.

clue.text: Beat up revolutionary students here

indicators.note: revolutionary, turning round, means the word up is read backwards

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics, where students study

explanation.surface: Radical students get beaten up by the police at a famous London college.
explanation.walkthrough: The London School of Economics was famous for student radicals in the 1960s, which is why 'revolutionary students' reads so naturally; 'revolutionary' actually works only on 'up', turning it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the rhythmic throb of the heart, a regular beat.

clue.text: Liberal essentially discharged cops when working

indicators.note: to cop is to catch or take, here taking a short word inside
discharged means emptied, so only the outside letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of essentially
as means when
a machine that is going is working

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician discharged police officers while they were at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' looks like a modifier, but it is the word to empty. 'Cops' looks like police but is the verb, to take in.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy-going people are relaxed and tolerant, which matches liberal in its sense of broad-minded.

clue.text: Puff away after cycling, speak and dry up

indicators.note: cycling a word moves its last letter round to the front

parts.note: to vape is to puff on an e-cigarette
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: After a bike ride, a smoker puffs, talks and runs out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: VAPE cycled moves its E to the front, giving EVAP, then ORATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that evaporates turns to vapour and disappears, so the verb means to dry up.

clue.text: Plan leapt out for one seeking a review

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A plan sprang forth to help someone looking for a second look.
explanation.definitionFit: An appellant is a party who appeals a court decision, asking a higher court for a review.

clue.text: Puts a spin on party accepting first of right-wing characters

indicators.note: a party that accepts others takes them in, holding them inside

parts.note: the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the opening letter of right
the letter S written out, as several characters

explanation.surface: A spin doctor tidies up a party that has welcomed some right-wing figures.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party, itself right-wing, which helps the surface. It holds R and ESSES, the S letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress something up is to present it more attractively than it deserves, which is putting a spin on it.

clue.text: Touch computer up to create recording device

parts.note: a touch of something is a dash of it

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: an Apple Mac is a computer

explanation.surface: Tap a computer to wake it so it starts recording.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashcam is a small video camera fixed to a car's dashboard to film the road.

clue.text: One likely to get you out and back to house — top dog

definitions.text: One likely to get you out

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of house
a top dog is the winner, the victor

explanation.surface: The leader of the pack is likely to chase you out and back to the house.
explanation.definitionFit: An evictor is a landlord or bailiff who removes tenants, forcing them out of a property.

clue.text: A-ha vocalist covering Confusion, …

indicators.note: a phrase that covers something conceals it within its letters

parts.note: the letters run across the band name and the next word

explanation.surface: The singer from the Norwegian band A-ha does a cover version of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses chain four clues into one story about a band; each clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Havoc is widespread disorder and chaos, so confusion is a looser synonym for it.

clue.text: Six-nil, fast and furious …

parts.note: the Roman numeral for six
a zero looks like O
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A six-nil scoreline, a fast and furious match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast and furious' reads as a phrase about pace, but fast is the Lenten fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent and furious both describe great force or rage, as in a violent or furious storm.

clue.text: … contest over, saving Tuchel's backside

indicators.note: saving here means except, so one letter is left out

parts.note: something over is finished, complete

indicators.note: the backside of a name is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of Tuchel

explanation.surface: A match is over, except that the England manager Thomas Tuchel is saved.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Tuchel is the German manager of the England football team.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete is to take part in a match, so the verb contest is a synonym.

clue.text: … small triumph, ending in prog rock

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a win is a triumph

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of prog

explanation.surface: A modest success for a progressive rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prog rock' reads as a music genre, but rock is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock is to move to and fro, as does something that swings, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Place with lots of scope to pursue cruises discussed

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so the piece for scope comes second
something discussed is talked about, so we go by how the word is said

parts.note: cruises at sea are sails
room for manoeuvre is scope

explanation.surface: A cruise ship offers plenty of space and many options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots' looks like plenty, but it means auction lots.
explanation.definitionFit: A salesroom is an auction room, where items are sold off in numbered lots.

clue.text: Name announced for monstrosity

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so we go by the sound of the word

parts.note: to cite someone is to name them

explanation.surface: A name is made public for an ugly building.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a sight is something ugly or ridiculous, as in 'you look a sight'.

clue.text: Odds on bunging in answer — slim

indicators.note: bunging something in is shoving it inside, between the other pieces

parts.note: starting price, the betting odds on a horse
re means on or about
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A punter bets on a horse with slim odds.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is the starting price, the odds at the start of a horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare can mean lean or thin, an adjective for a slim figure.

clue.text: Smart to turn down drop of schnapps after prune tart

indicators.note: after means placed later, behind the word for prune

parts.note: to prune a plant is to cut it back

indicators.note: turning something down is refusing it, so a letter of the drink is rejected
a drop is a tiny amount, the first letter only

parts.note: a wound that smarts stings
the first letter of schnapps

explanation.surface: Someone declines a schnapps after eating a prune tart, which would sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prune tart' reads as a dessert, but tart is the definition and prune a verb. STING loses its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart remark is sharp and hurtful, the same as a cutting one.

clue.text: University life expert hosting a show briefly

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: an ace is an expert
taken as written

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing a final letter

parts.note: a demo is a demonstration, a show

explanation.surface: A professor who is a top expert briefly hosts a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show briefly' looks like a short appearance, but it means a shortened word for a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the world of scholarship and universities, the academic environment as a whole.

clue.text: Great partner has strength to bed two Romeos

indicators.note: to bed something is to lay it inside, embedding it

parts.note: might is strength
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet, twice

explanation.surface: An ideal lover is strong enough to take two Romeos to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romeos' suggests lovers, which fits the surface, but each is just R.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Right is the ideal man to marry or settle down with, a perfect partner.

clue.text: Rigid structure of romance making American take a break

indicators.note: making the American do something means the letter for American is changed within the story
take here means the American letter gives way to the break, which takes its place

parts.note: a romance is a story or tale
a rest is a break

explanation.surface: A love affair forces a US citizen to step away from things for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: TALE is the romance; 'making American take a break' replaces its A (American) with REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a sturdy supporting frame, as under a table top or a bridge, so a rigid structure.
